clue.text: A frame-up that gets you anywhere

explanation.surface: A frame-up that opens every door sounds like a criminal's dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A frame-up' is not a stitch-up but a picture mount, and the second sense is the French name for a master key.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is both a mount or tape used to frame a picture and a master key that opens every lock.

clue.text: .Buttons on worker for display

parts.note: Buttons is the traditional nickname for a hotel page boy, from his uniform
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A uniformed page standing on a labourer to make a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttons' is a page boy, named for the rows of buttons on his uniform; 'on' puts him in front of the insect worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public show or spectacle, a display in the sense of a parade.

clue.text: 8, if successful, preparing for a rainy day

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper who succeeds is apparently also thinking ahead to bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the goalkeeper of 8-down: one who succeeds makes a save. The second sense is someone putting money by.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper who makes a stop is credited with a save, and someone putting money by for hard times is a thrifty depositor.

clue.text: They're full of praise for guests involved with oil

indicators.note: involved means mixed up or entangled, so the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Guests at a party mixed up with oil, perhaps a salad dressing mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles GUESTS and OIL together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people who deliver speeches of praise, typically at funerals, so they are full of compliments.

clue.text: Drops in at the sweetshop for something to bite

definitions.text: Drops in at the sweetshop for something to bite

parts.words: Drops in at the sweetshop for something to bite
parts.note: reads like popping into a shop for a snack, but means a tart boiled sweet sold as drops and a corrosive that bites into metal

explanation.surface: Someone pops into a sweetshop for a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops in' is not a visit but the sweets called acid drops, and a corrosive is said to bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangy boiled sweets are sold as acid drops, and a corrosive chemical is said to bite into metal.

clue.text: Whereby Father Neptune's income is retained

definitions.text: Whereby Father Neptune's income is retained

parts.words: Whereby Father Neptune's income is retained
parts.note: the sea god's income is the water that comes in from the sea, held back by a sluice that shuts as the sea falls

explanation.surface: A tax arrangement for the sea god's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Neptune's 'income' is the sea water coming in; a gate that lets it in then shuts as the sea ebbs holds it back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice gate that opens to let the flood in and closes against the ebb keeps the sea water in a basin or dock.

clue.text: Singularly trustworthy investments ?

parts.note: the investment funds are unit trusts, and read singularly each piece is one unit of the fund

explanation.surface: An investment that is exceptionally reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly' seems to mean exceptionally, but points to single pieces: a unit trust's holders own shares that are each one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Unit trusts are pooled investment funds, and what an investor buys are single shares of the fund.

clue.text: Partly described Lady Godiva's riding (even with a saddle)

definitions.text: Partly described Lady Godiva's riding (even with a saddle)

parts.words: Partly described Lady Godiva's riding (even with a saddle)
parts.note: the word for riding without a saddle also describes one part of the naked rider, who would be uncovered there even sitting on one

explanation.surface: An account of the famous naked ride through Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry; 'partly described' means the word describes one part of her, which was uncovered even if she had a saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding without a saddle has this name, and literally the word says the rider's back is uncovered.

clue.text: His, net receipts are losses

parts.note: reads like accounts where net income is a loss, but the net is a football net and what it receives are goals conceded

explanation.surface: A businessman whose net income is all losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net receipts' looks like accounting; the net is the one a keeper guards, and every goal it takes in is a loss to his side.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper guards the net, and every ball it receives is a goal against his team.

clue.text: Hammer type of inheritance

parts.note: a gavel is the small hammer of a judge or auctioneer
kind means type or sort

explanation.surface: A heavy kind of hammer passed down through the family.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old Kentish custom of land tenure under which an estate was shared equally among the heirs.

clue.text: Princess has house in state

parts.note: Princess Ida is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera

explanation.surface: A princess owns a house in some state or other.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan heroine; 'has' and 'in' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Waggoner goes, to the French and Latvian capital

parts.note: au is French for to the, as in au revoir
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A carter sets off for France and the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Waggoner is a constellation, the Charioteer, not a carter; 'goes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern constellation is known as the Charioteer or Waggoner.

clue.text: It may be cracked, but reveals a heart of gold

definitions.text: It may be cracked, but reveals a heart of gold

parts.words: It may be cracked, but reveals a heart of gold
parts.note: sounds like a tough character with a soft centre, but it is the casing round a golden yolk

explanation.surface: A gruff character who, once you get through, turns out kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'heart of gold' is the yellow yolk inside an egg once its casing is cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: The brittle casing of an egg is cracked open to reach the yellow yolk inside.

clue.text: A moist form of philosophy

indicators.note: form here means a shape or arrangement, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A damp school of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges the letters of A MOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese system of thought, founded on the Tao Te Ching, is a philosophy and religion.

clue.text: Show a treetop development

indicators.note: a development is something worked out into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A show staged up in the treetops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges A TREETOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera with spoken dialogue and songs is a stage show.

clue.text: Obstruction makes Wenceslas call a halt

parts.note: to stop is to call a halt
Good King Wenceslas in the Christmas carol has a page who follows him

explanation.surface: A good king brings matters to a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol 'Good King Wenceslas' the king calls out to his page; here he tells him to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockage or halt in a flow or process is an obstruction.

clue.text: Varsity Officer? No, Little Sister is the forecast

parts.note: prog is Oxford and Cambridge slang for a proctor, a university disciplinary officer
sis is a short form of sister

explanation.surface: A university proctor's refusal and a sibling's weather report.
explanation.walkthrough: A proctor is a university officer who keeps discipline; 'prog' is the students' word for him. 'Varsity' is British slang for university.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's prediction of how a disease will run is a forecast of its course.

clue.text: Gettin' fearfully wild, we hear, in the vessel

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is to be said out loud and taken for a word of like sound

parts.note: panickin' is a clipped form of panicking, getting wildly frightened

explanation.surface: Someone getting frantic inside a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g of 'Gettin'' shows the clipped form, panickin', which said out loud matches the word for a small pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A small metal drinking cup or pan is a vessel.

clue.text: He may be moved to sacrifice

definitions.text: He may be moved to sacrifice

parts.words: He may be moved to sacrifice
parts.note: reads as someone stirred to give himself up, but is a piece on a board pushed to a square where it will be taken

explanation.surface: A man so stirred that he gives himself up for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' is not stirred emotionally but pushed on a board, where a piece may be given away for advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece in the board game is moved by the player and may be given up deliberately to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Eggs some drivers do without

explanation.surface: Eggs, which some motorists manage without.
explanation.walkthrough: Drivers of automatic cars do without the pedal for changing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eggs laid at one time is a clutch, and automatic cars have no clutch pedal.

clue.text: Literary work that is in character of course

parts.note: a book is a literary work
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A novel that puts a familiar character in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means of the racecourse, not 'naturally': a betting man found at the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker taking bets is a familiar figure at the racecourse.

clue.text: The phantom or idol one wildly embraces

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the second word sits inside the first
wildly signals that the letters of one are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A ghost or a worshipped figure that someone hugs passionately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' turns ONE into EON, which 'embraces' IDOL; 'or' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Greek for an image and means a spectre or apparition.

clue.text: Non-stop like the Ring ?

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle feels as though it goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring has no end, and Wagner's Ring cycle is famously long.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuous without a break is non-stop, and a ring is a circle with no end point.

clue.text: Not that his pictures were of the ruder variety

definitions.text: Not that his pictures were of the ruder variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters of ruder are recast

explanation.surface: A defence of an artist whose work was never smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' asks for a different arrangement of RUDER, giving the German Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Durer was the German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: Snow White blushed, out West, to have done so asleep

indicators.note: out tells us to put the letter for West outside, removing it

parts.note: snow white means pure white, so white gives snow
someone who blushed went red

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale heroine turned pink in the west while sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes W (West) from SNOW, leaving SNO; then add RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing noisily while sleeping is what this verb records in the past tense.

clue.text: Sound critique of stage entertainment

indicators.note: Sound at the head of the clue means the next word's synonym is to be said out loud

parts.note: a review is a critique of a book or show

explanation.surface: A solid review of a theatrical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'solid', but signals that REVIEW said out loud gives the show's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A light stage show of sketches, songs and dances is this kind of entertainment.

clue.text: Madly keen for a bender

indicators.note: madly signals that the letters of keen are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Wildly enthusiastic about a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bender' looks like a drinking spree, but is the joint that bends the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint in the middle of the leg is what bends it, so it is a bender.

clue.text: Provide pussy with a capital, vis-a vis ?

definitions.text: pussy with a capital, vis-a vis ?

explanation.surface: Giving a cat some money to spend.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat with capital is a kitty, a pool of money; diagonally opposite is both kitty-corner and cater-corner, so this word stands to kitty as its twin.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply food or what is needed is to provide, and cater-corner is the old form of kitty-corner, meaning diagonally opposite.

clue.text: Case for a sovereign cure

parts.note: a case is a medical case, and a sovereign cure is a cure by the monarch's touch rather than a reliable remedy

explanation.surface: An argument for a guaranteed remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign cure' sounds like a sure remedy, but means one by a sovereign: scrofula was believed cured by the royal touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrofula, a tubercular swelling of the neck glands, was said to be cured by the touch of a monarch.

clue.text: Life being what he made it, it was the death of him

definitions.text: Life being what he made it, it was the death of him

parts.words: Life being what he made it, it was the death of him
parts.note: the scientist in Mary Shelley's novel created life, and the creature he made caused his death

explanation.surface: A gloomy reflection on a man whose way of living killed him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life being what he made it' sounds like a fatalistic proverb, but he literally made a living being, and it destroyed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's scientist animated a creature built from dead bodies, and that monster brought about his death.
